question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total passengers carried by public transport in Spain (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as reported in INE's Estadística de Transporte de Personas (Passenger Transport Statistics) provisional monthly data; measured as number of passengers (journeys/trips) recorded by
target.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Estadística de Transporte de Personas (ETP)
target.cadence: Monthly, provisional data published roughly two months after the reference month (provisional figure for month M typically released around end of month M+2)
target.caveats: Target period is in the future relative to the 2026-09-11 cutoff, so no August 2026 observation exists; estimate must be built from prior-year August levels, year-to-date 2026 momentum, and seasonal/calendar effects. candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total passengers will be close to the August 2025 level adjusted for the 2026 year-to-date growth trend; the same-month prior-year value plus recent YoY growth rates anchors the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP monthly total passengers (all transport classes combined) for August 2024, August 2025, and all months Jan-Jul 2026 (or latest available before cutoff), plus the YoY growth rate for each month of 2026 published before 2026-09-11. Minimum: August 2025 total and the most recent 2026 monthly YoY growth.

August 2024 growth by class (urban +5.8, interurban +7.1, special/discretionary -1.1) — prior-year seasonal context.
Monthly 2025 class-level YoY growth series from INE; internally consistent, showing strong April dip and mid-year rebound. Useful for momentum, not for August level.
February 2026 urban +2.0%, interurban -4.2% — the only 2026 momentum evidence; indicates slower 2026 growth than 2025.
November 2025 levels (thousands) and YoY: total 508.7m +4.5%, city 318.8m +6.8%, inter-city 143.6m +1.2%, special -0.6%. Gives class shares and late-2025 momentum.
October 2025 total +4.4%, city +5.4%, inter-city +3.6% — consistent with November pattern.

p49.role: Total public transport passengers in Spain, August 2025 (362.4 million), the base level

a1.role: Change factor from August 2025 to August 2026 for total public transport passengers

methods.rationale: Anchors on the observed August 2025 total level (p49) and applies a 2026 growth factor (a1) grounded in the 2025 growth rate (p20) and the decelerating 2026 signal (p55). Shared dependency: relies on the single INE August 2025 level; failure mode is that 2026 momentum differs materially from a1.

p49.role: Total public transport passengers in Spain, August 2025

p22.role: Special and discretionary passengers August 2025 (>21.6 million), used as the special/discretionary share of the total

a2.role: Change factor from August 2025 to August 2026 for special/discretionary transport

methods.rationale: Decomposes the total into the non-special/discretionary part (held flat at its August 2025 level) and the special/discretionary part (grown by a2). The special/discretionary share is derived from p22 relative to the sum of its sub-components p23+p24, applied to the total p49. This is a rough split because p22 is a rounded 'more than' figure and the urban/interurban remainder is assumed flat; failure mode is that urban/interurban also grow. It provides a class-aware cross-check on m1.

assumptions.name: August 2026 total YoY growth factor vs August 2025
assumptions.rationale: August 2025 total grew 2.6% (p20/p49); late-2025 momentum was stronger (Oct +4.4% p60, Nov +4.5% p56) but the only 2026 evidence (Feb 2026 urban +2.0%, interurban -4.2%, p55) points to deceleration. A central 2% growth with a wide range spanning flat-to-6% reflects this tension; it is a change factor, not a level.
assumptions.applies_when: August 2026 demand follows the decelerating 2026 trend implied by p55 rather than reverting to 2025's pace.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published March–July 2026 ETP growth returning to ~3–4% or turning negative.

assumptions.name: August 2026 special/discretionary YoY growth factor
assumptions.rationale: Special/discretionary grew 11.7% in Aug 2025 (p22) but only ~1% cumulatively Jan–Aug 2025 (p54) and -0.6% in Nov 2025 (p59); August is a tourism-heavy month so a modest positive growth is plausible, but the high 2025 base argues against repeating double digits.
assumptions.applies_when: Summer 2026 discretionary travel grows modestly over the strong August 2025 base.
assumptions.falsified_by: Summer 2026 tourism/coach data showing a sharp contraction or a repeat of double-digit growth.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
